title: Kakaki
summary: The kakaki is a very long metal trumpet blown at royal courts in the Sahel. Its narrow tube, as long as a person is tall or more, ends in a small bell, and its low, blaring note announces rulers. Players sound long notes in formal ensembles.
howToPlay: Four notes of the trumpet are lit along the tube, the higher ones nearer the mouthpiece.
A band of breath runs from the mouth to the note you strike, and rings of sound leave the bell.
Long notes swell slowly: strike close to the beat and let them ring.
rules: A call is a line of long notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It is played in formal court ensembles, where its long notes mark the arrival of a ruler.
